questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with a painless genital ulcer with a clean base and indurated edges. Dark-field microscopy shows spiral organisms. Which of the following is the first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. This is the CDC/WHO first-line recommendation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with verrucous nodules on the dorsum of the foot slowly enlarging over 2 years. Biopsy shows Medlar bodies (copper penny bodies). What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous fungi and shows pathognomonic Medlar bodies (muriform cells/copper penny bodies) on histopathology. Lesions are verrucous and slowly progressive.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal skin, positive Nikolsky sign is absent. Immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the basement membrane zone. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG + C3 at the BMZ on DIF. Target antigen is BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man with lepromatous leprosy is started on multidrug therapy. He develops sudden onset fever, tender erythematous nodules over the limbs, and nerve tenderness. ESR is elevated. What type of lepra reaction is this?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (Type 2 reaction) occurs in lepromatous/borderline lepromatous leprosy. It presents with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic symptoms. It is immune complex (Type III) mediated.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly papule with telangiectasias on his nose that has been slowly enlarging. Histopathology shows peripheral palisading of cells. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma on the nose (high-risk area) is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, which provides the highest cure rates with maximum tissue conservation.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with symmetric hypopigmented patches with loss of sensation over the trunk and upper limbs. Slit skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells. What is the leprosy type?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-defined hypopigmented patches with loss of sensation, negative SSS, and histopathology with well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans cells. Nerve involvement is prominent.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the penis following a new sexual contact. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The drug of choice for initial episode is:
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg 5 times daily for 10 days
questions.exp: Primary genital herpes (HSV-2) is treated with Valacyclovir 1g BD for 10 days (or Acyclovir 400 mg TDS for 7-10 days). Valacyclovir has better bioavailability and simpler dosing than acyclovir.

questions.q: A patient with psoriasis develops nail changes including onycholysis, subungual hyperkeratosis, and oil drop sign. The pathology underlying the 'oil drop sign' in psoriatic nails is:
opts: Psoriatic involvement of the nail matrix
Psoriatic involvement of the nail bed
Separation of nail plate from matrix
questions.exp: The salmon patch/oil drop sign in psoriasis is due to psoriatic involvement of the nail bed, producing a yellowish-brown discoloration visible through the nail plate. Matrix involvement causes pitting.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman with butterfly rash, photosensitivity, and joint pains is being evaluated for SLE. Anti-dsDNA antibodies are elevated. Which finding on skin biopsy with immunofluorescence would be most characteristic?
opts: Linear IgG at the basement membrane zone
Granular IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: Lupus band test (direct immunofluorescence) in SLE shows granular deposits of IgG, IgM, IgA, and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction (BMZ), present in both lesional and non-lesional sun-exposed skin.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-crusted lesions around the mouth and nose. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus. What is the preferred topical treatment for localized impetigo?
questions.exp: Mupirocin (pseudomonic acid) is the preferred topical antibiotic for impetigo caused by Staphylococcus aureus. It inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase and has excellent activity against S. aureus.

questions.q: A 35-year-old presents with annular scaly plaques on the trunk. KOH examination shows hyphae. The characteristic 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern on KOH/Wood's lamp fluorescence is seen in:
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia furfur) shows the characteristic 'spaghetti and meatballs' (short curved hyphae and budding spores) on KOH preparation. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man with chronic renal failure presents with pruritic, burning blisters on sun-exposed areas of the hands and face. Urine shows elevated porphyrins. The enzyme deficiency responsible is:
questions.exp: Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) results from deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase. It is the most common porphyria, presenting with skin fragility and blisters on sun-exposed areas, predominantly in adults.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man presents with perifollicular papules and pustules around the chin and cheeks after shaving. The causative organism most commonly responsible for folliculitis barbae is:
questions.exp: Sycosis barbae (folliculitis barbae) is caused by Staphylococcus aureus. It presents as recurrent perifollicular papules and pustules in the beard area of adult men.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with diffuse hair loss notices excessive shedding 3 months after childbirth. The type of alopecia she has is:
questions.exp: Telogen effluvium occurs 2-3 months after a triggering event (postpartum, febrile illness, surgery). Parturition is the most common cause. The precipitant shifts anagen follicles into telogen prematurely.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with violaceous flat-topped papules with Wickham's striae on the wrists and inner thighs. The proposed pathogenesis of lichen planus involves:
opts: CD8+ T cell-mediated cytotoxicity against basal keratinocytes
Immune complex deposition at dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: Lichen planus is a T-cell mediated lichenoid tissue reaction. CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes target basal keratinocytes displaying altered self-antigens, leading to apoptosis and characteristic histology.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl presents with comedones, papules, and pustules on the face. She has been on antibiotics for 6 months with partial response. What is the mechanism of action of isotretinoin in acne?
opts: Reduces sebaceous gland size and sebum production
questions.exp: Isotretinoin (oral retinoid) reduces sebaceous gland size by up to 90% and decreases sebum production. It also normalizes follicular keratinization and has anti-inflammatory effects.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive man develops extensive molluscum contagiosum lesions across the face. The CD4 count is 45 cells/μL. The treatment strategy that would most effectively reduce molluscum lesions is:
questions.exp: In HIV patients with low CD4 counts, extensive molluscum contagiosum is an immune reconstitution manifestation. Starting ART to restore immune function is the most effective long-term strategy.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with itchy blisters in the axillae and groin with mucosal involvement. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG (fish-net pattern). The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris with mucosal involvement targets desmoglein 3 (pemphaxin). DIF shows intercellular 'fish-net' IgG in the epidermis. Desmoglein 1 is targeted in pemphigus foliaceus (superficial type).

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a non-healing ulcerated nodule on the lower lip. It has everted margins and is indurated. Regional lymph nodes are palpable. Biopsy shows atypical squamous cells invading the dermis. The most important prognostic factor is:
questions.exp: In squamous cell carcinoma, regional lymph node metastasis is the single most important prognostic factor, reducing 5-year survival from ~90% (node-negative) to ~25-50% (node-positive).

questions.q: A 25-year-old man with a history of atopic dermatitis presents for patch testing. The most common allergen causing allergic contact dermatitis from rubber gloves is:
questions.exp: Thiurams (thiuram mix) are the most common cause of rubber-related contact allergy, as they are accelerators used in rubber vulcanization. Nickel is the most common allergen overall in patch testing.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with a skin lesion that looks like a bruise that won't heal on the leg. Dermoscopy shows a structureless red-blue-black area. Histology shows spindle cells lining vascular channels. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Classic Kaposi's sarcoma typically presents on lower extremities in elderly Mediterranean/Eastern European men. Histology shows spindle cells lining vascular spaces. HHV-8 is the causative agent.

questions.q: A dermatologist performs a punch biopsy under local anesthesia. The depth of local anesthetic infiltration for effective skin biopsy would be into the:
questions.exp: For dermatological procedures, local anesthetics should be infiltrated into the deep dermis or dermal-subcutaneous junction to adequately anesthetize skin. Intradermal injection causes a wheal and effective anesthesia.

questions.q: A 25-year-old pregnant woman presents with scabies. The safest topical treatment for scabies in pregnancy is:
questions.exp: Permethrin 5% cream is the safest and most effective treatment for scabies in pregnancy. Lindane is contraindicated in pregnancy due to neurotoxicity. Permethrin is category B (FDA).

questions.q: A 38-year-old man presents with erythematous, violaceous plaques with 'lilac heliotrope' discoloration around the eyes, Gottron's papules on knuckles, and proximal muscle weakness. The most specific antibody for dermatomyositis is:
questions.exp: Anti-Mi-2 is highly specific for dermatomyositis (classic phenotype with prominent skin features). Anti-Jo-1 is associated with antisynthetase syndrome (myositis + ILD + mechanic's hands).

questions.q: A Wood's lamp examination is performed. Which condition fluoresces with a coral-red color under Wood's lamp?
questions.exp: Erythrasma caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum produces coral-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp due to porphyrin production. Tinea capitis (Microsporum) fluoresces green; Pseudomonas shows green.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with depigmented patches on the face, hands, and around body orifices. Woods lamp shows chalk-white fluorescence. Dermoscopy shows perifollicular repigmentation. What is the mechanism of repigmentation in vitiligo?
opts: Migration of melanocytes from the dermal-epidermal junction
Activation of amelanotic melanocytes from outer root sheath of hair follicles
Migration of melanocytes from adjacent normal skin
questions.exp: In vitiligo, repigmentation occurs by activation of amelanotic melanocyte reservoirs in the outer root sheath (ORS) of hair follicles. This is why perifollicular pigmentation is first seen with PUVA/NB-UVB.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy presents with diffuse scaling of the scalp with broken-off hairs. Occipital lymphadenopathy is present. Fungal culture on Sabouraud's dextrose agar grows rapidly with a powdery surface. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Trichophyton tonsurans causes endothrix tinea capitis (black dot type) with broken hairs and diffuse scaling. It is the most common cause of tinea capitis in North America and is non-fluorescent under Wood's lamp.

questions.q: A 44-year-old woman develops a fixed drug eruption after taking NSAIDs. She notes the lesion always appears at the same site on her lip. The pathophysiology involves:
opts: Tissue-resident CD8+ T cells in the epidermis at that site
questions.exp: Fixed drug eruption (FDE) is mediated by tissue-resident memory CD8+ T cells (intraepidermal) that are activated by the drug. They produce interferon-gamma and TNF-alpha causing keratinocyte apoptosis at the same site each time.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a long-standing hyperpigmented plaque on the leg with irregular borders. Dermoscopy shows an atypical pigment network and regression structures. ABCDE criteria show asymmetry, border irregularity, multiple colors, diameter >6mm, and it has been evolving. Sentinel lymph node biopsy is recommended when Breslow thickness is:
questions.exp: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is recommended for melanoma with Breslow thickness > 1.0 mm, or > 0.8 mm with adverse features (ulceration, high mitotic rate). It is the most important staging procedure.

questions.q: A 23-year-old HIV-positive woman presents with whitish, non-removable plaques on the lateral borders of the tongue. The lesions persist despite antifungal therapy. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia (OHL) is caused by EBV replication in epithelial cells and presents as white non-removable plaques on lateral tongue borders. It is an AIDS-defining marker and does not respond to antifungals.

questions.q: A 42-year-old man undergoes Tzanck smear for a vesicular eruption. The smear is stained with Giemsa. Acantholytic cells (Tzanck cells) are characteristic of which group of disorders?
opts: Pemphigus vulgaris and herpes simplex/zoster infections
Epidermolysis bullosa and porphyria cutanea tarda
Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
questions.exp: Tzanck cells (acantholytic keratinocytes with large nuclei and perinuclear condensation) are seen in pemphigus vulgaris and herpesvirus infections (HSV/VZV). In herpes infections, multinucleated giant cells are also pathognomonic.
